week_in_brief: The channel boundaries are dissolving — delivery outpacing pickup, store space becoming a media asset, and prepared foods now competing directly with restaurants.

items.headline: Delivery Wins the Format War — Speed Isn't the Whole Answer
items.whats_happening: Same-day delivery now accounts for 65% of online grocery fulfillment (vs. 35% for pickup), driven by Walmart's 30-minute rollout in 33 markets and Amazon's 2,300-city expansion. But McKinsey's research shows consumers overwhelmingly prefer full assortment over ultra-fast delivery with limited selection. Meanwhile, Google restored the ability to create Dynamic Search Ads and delayed AI Max migration until February 2027, reinforcing that proven tactics still matter while automation stabilizes.
items.so_what: Don't race Walmart on speed. Invest in pickup networks and micro-fulfillment that protect margins and offer full assortment. DSAs remain a reliable backup while you test AI Max — keep both in rotation.

items.headline: Your Store Is Now a Media Channel
items.whats_happening: Physical store space is shifting from promotional zones to monetizable media assets. Brands are investing in 60–90 day experiential activations at front-of-store and inline zones, creating predictable revenue and dwell time. At the same time, TikTok expanded Symphony AI creative tools to generate platform-native video from text or images, enabling multi-location retailers to scale trend-responsive content without increasing budgets. Meta is now using third-party purchase and browsing data to personalize Feed content and AI responses across platforms.
items.so_what: Develop clear policies, pricing, and category protocols for in-store experiences — this is steady margin and engagement for regional chains competing with big-box assortment. Pair that with TikTok's video tools to turn those experiences into content at scale. Make sure your product catalog and event tracking are accurate; Meta's using that data for more than ads now.

items.headline: Prepared Foods and Private Label Aren't Support Categories Anymore
items.whats_happening: 25% of consumers now buy grocery-prepared foods as a restaurant substitute, with younger shoppers leading the shift. Walmart is promoting family meals under $10; Sam's Club expanded fresh and launched fruit-chopping programs. Prepared foods drive the highest trip frequency. Meanwhile, private label hit 50% unit share across Europe's largest markets, with consumers no longer seeing quality gaps between store brands and nationals. Google also launched Generative AI Performance Reports in Search Console, making AEO quantifiable — you can now track visibility across traditional search and AI Overviews in one dashboard.
items.so_what: Treat prepared foods and private label as profit and loyalty drivers, not loss leaders. Invest in hot bars, deli innovation, and premium private label positioning. Track your AI search visibility alongside organic — it's finally measurable.

items.headline: Omnichannel Shoppers Spend 31% More — Build for That
items.whats_happening: McKinsey data shows omnichannel shoppers (in-store + online) spend 31% more than single-channel customers. Delivery growth is outpacing pickup 3:1. This isn't a defensive channel — it's a growth engine. Google's June spam update (completed June 24–26) emphasized quality, speed, mobile usability, and expert trust as core ranking signals. LinkedIn upgraded search with AI-powered conversational intent matching, prioritizing credible profiles with demonstrated authority over keyword-stuffed bios.
items.so_what: Design omnichannel strategies that serve multiple missions — quick trips, big baskets, delivery, pickup, in-store. Invest in inventory visibility and unified loyalty. Make sure your site is fast, mobile-optimized, and substantive. If your team has B2B roles, focus LinkedIn profiles on specific expertise and proof, not keywords.

this_weeks_take: The grocery store is no longer just a place to buy food. It's a media channel, a fulfillment node, and a restaurant competitor. Regional grocers who treat these as integrated systems — not separate problems — will capture wallet share that nationals can't.
